reason: This passage (Exodus 2:16-22) is a personal narrative describing Moses' encounter with the daughters of Reuel (Jethro), a Midianite priest. It recounts Moses defending the daughters from rival shepherds, his acceptance of hospitality, and his marriage to Zipporah. The text contains no discussion of Hebrew leadership, the state of the Hebrew people, or any accountability issues related to them. The passage focuses entirely on private, domestic matters and predates Moses' emergence as a leader of the Hebrew people.
